decisions.statement: Every page naming a page by a bare name under the key is answered in this one answer.
Which pages name a page by a bare name is read from the values the index files.
Which values a key's entries beside the page carry is read from that file rather than the index.
The pages written are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath it.
The page type written is the one the page reached is of.
That page type is read off the page reached rather than off what the property declares.
The page type of the page reached is read off the name of that page's file.
Every file the key's values sit in is written, and no file but those.
A name already stating its page type is passed over.
A name that is an id is passed over.
A name reaching no page refuses the whole change.
A name reaching more than one page refuses the whole change.
A refusal names the page that drew the refusal.
A key declaring no page type to reach is refused.
What a key declares is read off the property page that key names rather than off the key.
A key the page type declares nowhere is refused.
A field named beside the key is written inside each of that key's entries.
What a field declares is read off the record property or the entry shape the key names.
A field the record property or the entry shape declares nowhere is refused.
A run naming no field writes the key's own value.
A key whose values sit in a file beside the page is written there, and the page's body is not.
Every part of that file is written.
A row whose field holds no text is passed over.
No rung beneath is reached.
Nothing here writes the property's declaration.
No name is written with a scope.
A key of the same name inside a value a row states is left as it is.
A row's keys are left as they are.

definition: a bare name written anew with the page type it reaches, on every page of one page type
